_note: Editorial narrative arcs for native series — how the texts fit together as a possible sermon series, broken into BEATS (movements over week-ranges). A Sunday's beat = the movement whose [from,to] covers its week (series.py attaches it to membership). Keyed by series id (year-role-bookcode-firstocc). AI-drafted, Wilson curates.

a-second-rom-proper-5-10-a.arc: Paul's letter to the Romans, read straight through, is already a series — from the plight and gift of justification, through life in the Spirit and God's faithfulness to Israel, to the transformed common life.

beats.label: Justified & freed (Rom 4–6)
beats.note: Abraham's faith, peace with God, and the turn from death-in-sin to life-in-God.

beats.label: Life in the Spirit (Rom 7–8)
beats.note: The war within, no condemnation, and nothing able to separate us from the love of God.

beats.label: God's faithfulness to Israel (Rom 9–11)
beats.note: The hard mystery of election — and a mercy that finally reaches all.

beats.label: Living sacrifice (Rom 12–13)
beats.note: Bodies offered as worship; love named as the fulfilling of the law.

a-first-gen-trinity-sunday-a.arc: The book of Genesis walked in order across the summer — creation, the promise to Abraham, the flawed and chosen line of Jacob, and Joseph's providence: the whole story of the promise carried through unlikely people.

beats.label: In the beginning (Gen 1)
beats.note: Creation, blessing, and rest — the ground the whole story stands on.

beats.label: The call & testing of Abraham (Gen 12–22)
beats.note: Promise made and promise threatened, up to the binding of Isaac.

beats.label: Jacob, wrestling toward blessing (Gen 24–32)
beats.note: Rebekah, the stolen birthright, the ladder at Bethel, the night at the Jabbok.

beats.label: Joseph — evil turned to good (Gen 37–45)
beats.note: Sold by his brothers, and yet God meaning it for good.
